title: Do not turn a delayed shrink-regrow clamp into upward reader input
outcome: Review at HEAD 7acacc1. A temporary real-scroll-hook probe first explicitly navigates to bottom(top800, scrollHeight1000, clientHeight200, FOLLOW=true), then models browser-only geometry1000->600->1000 with clamp top400 and delivers the delayed native scroll event after regrowth, without any wheel/key/pointer/focus input. SessionPaneView.scroll.ts:2619-2667 sees final height >= recorded height and top400 not at final bottom; because no active virtualizedBottomBoundaryReveal flag exists, movedUpFromRecordedPosition becomes true. Lines2753-2778 synthesize user navigation, detach FOLLOW and cancel settling. Probe expects FOLLOW to remain true and fails false. This is distinct from the viewport-height-only clamp already tracked in .26: final geometry equals the old geometry, hiding an intermediate content collapse. Existing boundary test explicitly covers protection only while boundary-reveal flag is active; its finished variant accepts detachment without reader input. This is a proven handler-level vulnerability consistent with transient layout around Stop/hydration, NOT an end-to-end reproduction of Greg pressing Stop or a measurement of his live browser. Temporary diagnostic probe removed; no production changes.
acceptance: A shrink/regrow plus delayed native scroll with no reader gesture preserves explicit FOLLOW both during and after boundary reveal; subsequent real output follows. Real upward wheel/key/touch/scrollbar/focus navigation still wins immediately. Cover delayed native events and lifecycle-driven layout; do not infer user intent solely from two geometry snapshots.
